stories.title: SP may reduce Muslim candidates in 2027 polls:Akhilesh reshapes public image through religious visits; to follow pandits' advice
stories.summary: Ahead of the 2027 Uttar Pradesh Assembly elections, Samajwadi Party chief Akhilesh Yadav is trying to change his political image. The SP has long been seen as a party focused mainly on Muslim and Yadav voters, while the BJP has often targeted this perception during elections. Now, Akhilesh is attempting to create a new image by building the Kedareshwar temple in Etawah. He also claims that he plans his daily routine according to the advice of priests and astrologers. Political experts believe the SP may give more importance to upper caste leaders in the 2027 elections instead of relying heavily on Muslim candidates. This political shift in the SP has become more visible after the heavy defeat of the Trinamool Congress in the West Bengal elections. First, let's understand Akhilesh's image, which he inherited As soon as he took over the party, Akhilesh managed Muslim, Yadav voters Akhilesh Yadav inherited this image. After ordering firing on karsevaks in Ayodhya in 1990, the BJP started calling Mulayam Singh 'Mullah Mulayam'. After this, SP's identity became based on the Muslim-Yadav (M-Y) equation. When Akhilesh took over the party's command, he was seen as the protector of this very vote bank. Muzaffarnagar riots, BJP's allegations - soft stance for a particular community The Muzaffarnagar riots of 2013, during Akhilesh's tenure as Chief Minister, further strengthened this image. The SP government had issued a notification to provide compensation of Rs 5 lakh each only to riot-affected Muslims. This decision had to be withdrawn after the intervention of the Supreme Court. The BJP had alleged that the Akhilesh government adopted a soft stance towards the Muslim community. In March 2014, the Supreme Court also acknowledged that the government had largely failed to prevent the violence. After the Muzaffarnagar riots, a message went among Hindus that the SP government was biased towards Muslims. Now an attempt to change the image Kedareswar being built on the lines of Kedarnath Akhilesh Yadav is building 'Shri Kedareswar Mahadev Temple' in Etawah on the lines of Kedarnath temple in Uttarakhand. Akhilesh is the chief trustee of the temple. The temple is being built on the 'Shivshakti Aksh Rekha', which makes it religiously significant. Senior journalist Akhilesh Bajpai says - There is a plan to inaugurate this temple in the election year. Through this, Akhilesh wants to break the BJP's narrative, in which he is portrayed as anti-Hindu or only a benefactor of Muslims. Building a temple like Kedarnath is clearly part of a strategy to respond to BJP's Hindutva agenda. It is a different matter that Akhilesh has avoided visiting the two main Hindu temples in UP, Shri Krishna Janmabhoomi (Mathura) and Ram Mandir (Ayodhya). However, he did go for a Ganga bath during the Mahakumbh. Strategy to be decided on the suggestion of pundits and astrologers Akhilesh's press conference on May 6 surprised everyone in political circles. He had said, "Now I am taking every step on 'Pandit ji's' advice. In 2012, my government was formed under the guidance of Pandits and astrologers. Now I am walking on the same path again." Senior journalist Siddharth Kalhans says, "Akhilesh is saying that when to leave home, what color to wear, and even when to start election campaigning, all this will be decided by his astrologers." Through this, Akhilesh is trying to appease the Brahmin community. He is presenting himself as a protector of Sanatani traditions by raising issues like the insult of Brahmins and Shankaracharya. Expansion of PDA beyond the Muslim-Yadav factor Senior journalist Akhilesh Bajpai says - Akhilesh has understood that it is no longer easy to reach power in UP with the help of the Muslim-Yadav (M-Y) equation. Until the 2022 assembly elections, SP's focus remained on this equation, but they lost. In the 2024 Lok Sabha elections, Akhilesh gave the slogan of 'PDA' (Pichda, Dalit, Alpasankhyak - Backward, Dalit, Minority). By giving fewer tickets to Yadavs and Muslims, he bet on other backward castes and Dalits. This experiment was quite successful. BJP suffered a major dent and SP emerged as the largest party in UP. Now Akhilesh is expanding this formula in 2027. He is resorting to soft Hindutva to include upper castes in it. Possibility of major upheaval in ticket distribution Sources associated with SP say that the number of Muslim candidates may be reduced in the 2027 assembly elections. In the 2024 elections, out of SP's 62 candidates, only 4 were Muslim. The same formula may be applied in 2027 as well. Akhilesh believes that fielding more Muslim candidates will make it easier for BJP to polarize the elections. By giving fewer tickets to the Muslim community and associating himself with temples and Brahmins, Akhilesh is trying to breach a strong fortress of BJP. However, this strategy is also risky, as minority votes might scatter if tickets are reduced. Owaisi-Mayawati can harm SP Siddharth Kalahans says - The biggest challenge in front of Akhilesh's new strategy is Asaduddin Owaisi and Mayawati. If SP distances itself from the Muslim community or gives them fewer tickets, then Owaisi's AIMIM and BSP will try to fill this void. Owaisi has caused similar damage to opposition parties in Bihar, Maharashtra and Bengal. The direct benefit of scattered Muslim votes goes to BJP. BJP's New Strategy to Corner After the 2024 Victory Senior journalist Akhilesh Bajpai states - BJP had suffered losses in the 2024 Lok Sabha elections. To compensate for the losses incurred due to the narrative of changing the constitution and the slogan of '400 paar' (crossing 400 seats), BJP is now working more aggressively at the booth level. However, the circumstances of the Lok Sabha elections were different. There, SP benefited from BJP's strategic mistakes, but assembly elections are fought on local issues. This is why Akhilesh is now establishing himself as a leader of all communities. Taking the help of astrology and giving importance to Brahmins is an attempt to break BJP's strategy to corner. Meanwhile, Siddharth Kalahans believes that Akhilesh's path of soft Hindutva is both his political compulsion and a well-thought-out strategy. UP has now become the center of polarized politics, where the contest is directly between SP and BJP. Amidst Mayawati's declining support base, Akhilesh is presenting himself as the only alternative to the BJP. Through building temples, astrologers' advice, and new ticket equations, he is hoping for a return to power in 2027. This strategy is quite different from 2022. Because now Akhilesh is not just doing politics of opposition, but is on the path of countering BJP's agenda in his own way. It will be interesting to see whether UP likes SP's 'new avatar' or not?

stories.title: Shah fulfils promise by making Manoj Pandey minister:Yogi cabinet filled to full strength for first time, OBC ministers rise to 25
stories.summary: The Yogi Adityanath government carried out its second cabinet expansion on Sunday, filling all 60 ministerial posts for the first time in the Chief Minister’s nine-year tenure. The reshuffle is being viewed as the BJP’s final political groundwork ahead of the 2027 Uttar Pradesh Assembly elections. The expansion rewarded loyal leaders, addressed caste equations and attempted to strengthen the BJP’s support base across Purvanchal, Western UP, Awadh and Bundelkhand. Through the induction of OBC, Dalit and regional leaders, the BJP also tried to counter the Samajwadi Party’s PDA formula, 'Pichda, Dalit, Alpsankhyak' (Backward, Dalit and Minority). BJP counters Akhilesh Yadav’s PDA strategy The Samajwadi Party has been trying to unite backward classes and Dalits under its PDA campaign. To respond to this, the BJP included three OBC faces and two Dalit leaders in the cabinet expansion. The BJP wants to send a message that backward and Dalit communities are not only being respected but are also getting a fair share in power. The party believes this move will strengthen its hold among caste groups that could otherwise shift towards the SP. After the expansion, the number of OBC ministers increased from 22 to 25. General category ministers rose from 21 to 22. The number of Brahmin ministers increased from seven to eight, while Dalit ministers rose from eight to ten. The cabinet also includes one Sikh, one Muslim and one Scheduled Tribe minister. Cabinet expansion after more than 2 years This is the first cabinet expansion in more than two years. Political experts believe there has been no major ideological change, but the BJP has clearly focused on caste and regional representation. The reshuffle also reflects continuity in the party’s social engineering strategy. Bhupendra Chaudhary returns to cabinet Jat leader Bhupendra Chaudhary has been rewarded for maintaining close ties with the BJP’s central leadership. Chaudhary was made BJP state president in 2022 and had stepped down from his ministerial role at that time. He has now returned to the cabinet. In Western UP, Chaudhary is considered one of the BJP’s strongest Jat leaders. Unlike senior Jat minister Laxmi Narayan Chaudhary, who has earlier been associated with several parties including the SP, BSP, Congress and RLD, Bhupendra Chaudhary is seen as a core BJP cadre leader. He earlier served as Minister of State for PWD in Yogi Adityanath’s first term and was later promoted as Panchayati Raj Minister in 2019. In the second Yogi government, he again handled the Panchayati Raj portfolio before becoming the BJP state president on August 25, 2022. He remained state president until December 14, 2025. With his inclusion, the Yogi cabinet now has three Jat ministers, Bhupendra Chaudhary, Sugarcane Development Minister Laxmi Narayan Chaudhary and Minister of State KP Malik. Amit Shah keeps promise to Manoj Pandey The induction of Manoj Pandey is being seen as the fulfilment of a promise made by Union Home Minister Amit Shah. Pandey, formerly an SP MLA from Unchahar, rebelled during the Rajya Sabha elections in February 2024. He voted in favour of the BJP and reportedly helped six other SP MLAs support the party as well. At the time, Amit Shah had assured him of a ministerial role in the UP government. During the 2024 Lok Sabha elections, Shah shared the stage with Manoj Pandey in Raebareli, where Pandey formally joined the BJP. Shah had also visited his residence. BJP strengthens Brahmin representation Manoj Pandey is considered an influential Brahmin face in both Awadh and Purvanchal. He has often spoken openly for Brahmin rights and publicly opposed controversial remarks made by former minister Swami Prasad Maurya against Brahmins and Sanatan Dharma. The BJP believes his inclusion could reduce dissatisfaction among Brahmin voters in Awadh and eastern UP. The move also sends a message that Brahmin dissatisfaction did not damage the BJP politically. Earlier, Jitin Prasada had represented the Brahmin quota in the state cabinet before being moved to the Centre after becoming an MP from Pilibhit. The BJP now has three prominent Brahmin faces in UP politics, Deputy CM Brajesh Pathak, Union Minister of State Jitin Prasada and newly inducted minister Manoj Pandey. Lodh community given greater representation The BJP also addressed concerns within the Lodh community. Leaders such as Dharampal Singh, BL Verma and Rajveer Singh, son of former CM Kalyan Singh, were considered contenders for BJP state president. However, the party eventually appointed Kurmi leader Pankaj Chaudhary. This reportedly created resentment among Lodh leaders, who argued that Kurmis had stronger representation in government. To balance this, Kailash Rajput from the Lodh community was inducted as minister. The cabinet now has three Lodh ministers, Dharampal Singh, Sandeep Singh and Kailash Rajput. Vishwakarma Community gets representation Hansraj Vishwakarma, a close aide of Prime Minister Narendra Modi and former BJP district president in Varanasi, has also been made a minister. The Vishwakarma community has a sizeable presence in UP but previously lacked cabinet representation. With his inclusion, there are now four ministers from Varanasi in the Yogi cabinet, Anil Rajbhar, Ravindra Jaiswal, Dayashankar Mishra Dayalu and Hansraj Vishwakarma. BJP plays ‘Pasi Woman Card’ The BJP also attempted to strengthen its Dalit and women's outreach by inducting Krishna Paswan. The Pasi community has long been seen as a BJP support base. Party leaders reportedly feared the vote bank could weaken if the community did not receive stronger representation before 2027. By appointing Krishna Paswan, the BJP believes it has simultaneously addressed Dalit, Pasi and women representation. Valmiki Community strengthened further The BJP also strengthened its outreach among Valmiki voters by appointing Surendra Diler as minister. The Valmiki community is considered an important BJP support base among Dalits. After former minister Anoop Valmiki became an MP from Hathras, the Khair Assembly by-election was won by Surendra Diler, son of late MP Rajiv Diler. His induction ensures continued Valmiki representation in the cabinet. 2 ministers promoted Ajit Pal Singh and Somendra Tomar were promoted as Ministers of State (Independent Charge). Ajit Pal Singh’s promotion is aimed at retaining support from the Pal community, which both the SP and BSP are trying to attract. Somendra Tomar’s elevation comes as the SP attempts to strengthen support among Gurjars in Western UP. Women still underrepresented Despite Krishna Paswan’s induction, women remain underrepresented in the cabinet. The Yogi government now has six women ministers out of 60, making women’s representation just 10%. The women ministers include Baby Rani Maurya, Gulab Devi, Rajni Tiwari, Pratibha Shukla, Vijay Lakshmi Gautam and Krishna Paswan. Youngest cabinet so far The current cabinet is younger than Yogi Adityanath’s first government. In 2022, the average age of ministers was 55 years. It has now dropped to 52.8 years. Surendra Diler, aged 33, is the youngest minister in the cabinet, while Dr Arun Kumar Saxena, aged around 74, is the oldest.

stories.title: Bike crashes into truck in Bulandshahar:Husband, wife and 3 children die, family was returning from relatives’ house
stories.summary: Five members of a family, including a husband, wife and their three children, were killed after their motorcycle rammed into the rear of a truck in Bulandshahr on Friday evening. The accident took place around 5:30 pm on National Highway-34 in the Dehat Kotwali area. Following the incident, the truck driver fled from the spot with the vehicle. According to police, Uttam Singh (45), a resident of Dhameda Keerat village, had borrowed a motorcycle to visit relatives in Khurja. He had reportedly told the owner that he would return after completing some work. His wife Urmila (40) and their three children, Nishant (8), Disha (6) and Anayra (4), were travelling with him on the same motorcycle. The family was returning home after meeting relatives when the accident occurred. First, see two pictures Motorcycle crashed into truck after it slowed suddenly Police said a truck travelling ahead near Bhaisauli Cut was moving at around 70 kmph when it suddenly slowed down. Uttam Singh’s motorcycle, which was reportedly travelling at high speed behind the truck, lost balance and crashed into the rear of the vehicle. The impact threw the entire family onto the road. Eyewitnesses said the bodies of the husband, wife and children were found piled on top of one another, while the motorcycle lay nearby with its front portion badly damaged. Uttam Singh worked in a private company Uttam Singh was employed at a private company in Secunderabad. He had travelled to Khurja to meet relatives and had borrowed the motorcycle from an acquaintance for the trip. Their eldest son Nishant studied in Class 3, daughter Disha in Class 2, while youngest daughter Anayra was studying in Class 1. The family includes Uttam Singh’s parents, brother, sister-in-law and sister. Police informed the relatives about the accident, though family members had not reached the spot immediately after the incident. SSP and senior officers reached accident site After receiving information, Senior Superintendent of Police Dinesh Kumar Singh, SP City Abhishek Pratap and CO City Prakhar Pandey reached the scene. Police shifted all five victims to hospital, where doctors declared them brought dead. Truck seized, driver absconding Following the crash, the truck driver attempted to flee with the vehicle. Police chased the truck, after which the driver abandoned it and escaped. SSP Dinesh Kumar Singh said the truck bears a Haryana registration number and has been seized by police. He added that all five bodies have been sent for post-mortem examination and efforts are underway to arrest the driver.

stories.title: 2 youths die inside septic tank in Lucknow:One enters first for cleaning, second follows him after seeing no activity
stories.summary: Two labourers died while cleaning a septic tank in Lucknow on Friday afternoon. The incident took place in Navipanah village under the Mal police station area, around 35 km from the district headquarters. According to initial information, labourer Rinku first entered the septic tank for cleaning work. When there was no sound or movement from him for a long time, another labourer, Rajesh, went inside the tank to check on him. However, no response was received from either of them afterwards, triggering panic among people present at the spot. Villagers and police pulled both out unconscious Locals immediately informed the Dial 112 police. With the help of the police team and villagers, both labourers were pulled out of the tank in an unconscious condition. They were rushed to hospital, where doctors declared both of them dead. See 3 pictures- Poisonous gas suspected inside tank Police suspect that poisonous gas inside the septic tank may have caused both labourers to lose consciousness, leading to their deaths. However, officials said the exact cause of death will only be confirmed after the post-mortem report is received. Following the incident, grief spread among the families of the deceased. Inspector Nawab Ahmed of Mal police station said- Two labourers died while cleaning a septic tank. stories.title: UP Evening Wrap:Cracks emerge in Taj Mahal’s Royal Gate after storms and heavy rain; Suvendu named new CM of West Bengal
stories.summary: Bhaskar English brings you the biggest news from Uttar Pradesh and around the world. Here are the top news headlines- 1. Suvendu Adhikari elected new Chief Minister of West Bengal The BJP legislature party elected Suvendu Adhikari as the next Chief Minister of West Bengal during a meeting in Kolkata. Union Home Minister Amit Shah formally announced his name after the party’s victory. 2. Akhilesh meets Mamata and Stalin, says allies are not abandoned in difficult times SP chief Akhilesh Yadav met Mamata Banerjee in Kolkata and reiterated support to alliance partners after the election results. He later shared photographs with Mamata and Tamil Nadu CM Stalin. 3. Cracks emerge in Taj Mahal’s Royal Gate after storms and heavy rain Visible deterioration has appeared at the Taj Mahal’s historic Royal Gate, with cracks developing and stones shifting from their original positions. The damage reportedly worsened following recent storms and rainfall. 4. TVK set to form government in Tamil Nadu, Vijay likely to be next CM Support from Congress, VCK, CPI and CPI(M) has reportedly strengthened Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam’s numbers after the Assembly election results. Vijay now appears poised to lead the next government in the state. 5. UP government orders conversion of prepaid smart meters into postpaid system The Uttar Pradesh government has directed power departments to convert prepaid electricity meters into postpaid meters. Consumers will also be allowed to clear pending bills till April in ten instalments. 6. Police encounters of child-crime accused raise questions over emerging pattern in UP Within hours of a child rape and murder case in Hardoi, police shot dead the accused in an encounter. The incident marks the third such police killing involving crimes against children in Uttar Pradesh within a month. 7. Iran seizes oil tanker, accuses vessel of disrupting country’s oil exports Iran has seized an oil tanker amid rising tensions with the United States despite claims of a ceasefire remaining in effect. The US military also carried out retaliatory strikes targeting sites linked to attacks on its forces. 8. Prayagraj girl’s skeletal remains found 17 days after alleged murder by boyfriend The skeletal remains of a Class 9 student were recovered from a bushy area in Prayagraj more than two weeks after she allegedly died. Police suspect her 17-year-old boyfriend was involved in the murder. 9. Smart meter backlash may trigger UP cabinet reshuffle, AK Sharma under pressure Public anger over prepaid smart electricity meters has reportedly forced the UP government to reconsider its policy. BJP and RSS leaders are said to have warned the issue could hurt the party electorally. 10. Centre plans major overhaul of 15 lakh government schools from May 2026 The Centre is preparing sweeping reforms aimed at strengthening governance in government schools across India. School Management Committees and parents may get greater control over budgets and expenditure decisions.

stories.title: 'We do not abandon allies in difficult times':Akhilesh meets Mamata and Stalin after election results, shares photos
stories.summary: Samajwadi Party chief Akhilesh Yadav met outgoing chief minister Mamata Banerjee during a courtesy visit to her Kolkata residence on Thursday. Reiterating his continued support to her, Yadav said he or his party never abandon allies during difficult times. “We are not the ones who abandon people in difficult times,” Akhilesh said. The UP leader also shared photographs of his meetings with Mamata and M.K. Stalin in a X post. Akhilesh last met Stalin during an INDIA alliance meeting ahead of the 2024 Lok Sabha elections. Mamata received Akhilesh at the gate When Akhilesh reached Mamata’s residence, Mamata herself came to the gate to receive him. As Akhilesh moved forward to present her with a shawl, Mamata said, “What was the need for this?” To this, Akhilesh replied, “Didi, you fought, you have not lost.” Om Prakash Rajbhar takes a dig Reacting to the meeting, Uttar Pradesh minister Om Prakash Rajbhar mocked the two leaders. He said Akhilesh had gone to console Mamata by saying, “You have lost only once, while we have lost twice. Let us come together and begin a new series of defeats.” Rajbhar also claimed that when the Bengal election results were being declared, Akhilesh remained silent for four hours and only later decided to meet Mamata. First, see photos that Akhilesh posted- Mamata had earlier refused the visit Akhilesh was initially scheduled to visit Bengal on May 5, immediately after the election results were announced. However, Mamata reportedly asked him not to come at that time. Although Akhilesh did not campaign in the Bengal elections, he continued supporting Mamata through social media posts during the campaign period. First meeting after election defeat This was the first meeting between Mamata and any INDIA alliance leader after the Trinamool Congress defeat in the Bengal elections. Before this, Mamata and Akhilesh had last met on January 27. Political observers consider the renewed interaction between the Samajwadi Party and Trinamool Congress significant ahead of the 2027 Uttar Pradesh Assembly elections. 2 pictures of Mamata-Akhilesh meeting- TMC and DMK suffered major defeats In West Bengal, the BJP won 207 seats, while the Trinamool Congress was reduced to 80 seats. Compared with the 2021 elections, the BJP’s vote share increased by around 8%. Out of 119 seats that the TMC had consistently won for the past 15 years, the BJP captured 75 seats. This means the TMC lost nearly 63% of its traditional strongholds. Meanwhile, in Tamil Nadu, actor Vijay’s TVK secured 108 seats, while the DMK won 59 seats and the AIADMK secured 47. What does Akhilesh’s post indicate? Political analysts believe Akhilesh Yadav is trying to send a message of opposition unity by publicly standing with both Mamata Banerjee and MK Stalin. Senior journalist Rajendra Kumar said Akhilesh’s political style shows that once he aligns with someone, he generally avoids publicly attacking them, even after failed alliances. He pointed to the 2017 alliance between the Samajwadi Party and Congress, which performed poorly in elections. Despite the setback, Akhilesh did not make statements against Congress that could damage relations between the parties. The same pattern was seen after the 2019 alliance with Mayawati. Even after the alliance collapsed, Akhilesh refrained from criticising either Mayawati or the BSP. Rajendra Kumar added that Akhilesh’s restraint helped him gain support among Scheduled Caste voters. He also noted that even after the successful opposition alliance in the 2024 elections, several Congress leaders made controversial remarks against Akhilesh and the Samajwadi Party. Despite this, neither Akhilesh nor his party leaders responded aggressively. According to Rajendra Kumar, Akhilesh is attempting to project himself as a major opposition face who maintains cordial relations with all opposition parties, making him acceptable as a future national leader if such an opportunity arises. BJP says ‘Sad people met to wipe each other’s tears’ BJP leaders strongly criticised the meeting between Akhilesh and Mamata-

stories.title: Crack emerges in Taj Mahal’s historic Royal Gate:Stones fall from monument during storms and rain
stories.summary: The Taj Mahal, regarded as one of the most beautiful monuments in the world, is now showing visible signs of deterioration. The Royal Gate, also known as the Shahi Darwaza, has developed cracks in several places, while many stones have shifted from their original positions. The condition of the gate has become so fragile that it is no longer able to withstand storms and heavy rain. During recent spells of bad weather, stones from the structure broke off and fell twice. On several occasions, tourists narrowly escaped injury. This is not the first such incident. In recent years, stones, railings and jalis across different sections of the Taj Mahal complex have also collapsed or broken due to weakening structures and weather damage. Recent incidents at the Taj Mahal April 7, 2026- A powerful storm and heavy rain struck Agra. During the storm, white and red stones from the Royal Gate came loose and fell. Fortunately, no tourists were injured. April 30, 2026- Even a comparatively mild storm and rainfall proved too much for the weakened structure of the Royal Gate. Five pieces of white stone broke off and fell to the ground. Earlier incidents May 31, 2024- A stone from the Royal Gate broke and fell. December 20, 2024- Stones detached and fell from the wall of the Southern Gate of the Taj Mahal complex. May 29, 2020- Marble and red sandstone jalis in the Taj Mahal complex were damaged and broken. During the same incident, the Western Gate became tilted after one of its hinges broke. These incidents are only a few examples. Stones and lattice structures at the monument have reportedly broken and fallen multiple times over the years. Royal Gate in dilapidated condition The Royal Gate, considered the main entrance to the Taj Mahal, is now visibly deteriorating. Stones have loosened in several areas, while cracks can clearly be seen across sections of the walls. Many stones have weakened with age and are gradually detaching from the structure. The red sandstone gate also contains white and black stones used for decorative carvings, many of which are now falling out. In several places, gaps have formed in the walls where stones have collapsed. White and black decorative stones have also started coming loose from the structure. 4 pictures of the dilapidated Royal Gate- History of the Royal Gate The Royal Gate serves as the principal entrance to the Taj Mahal complex. After entering through the eastern or western gates, visitors reach the forecourt and then proceed to the main mausoleum through this gate. Earlier, tourists entering through the southern gate also approached the monument through the Royal Gate. However, the southern gate has remained closed since 2018. Historians believe the Royal Gate is as old as the main mausoleum itself and was constructed during the same phase of development. What historians and experts say ? Historian Rajkishore Raje said the Royal Gate was built alongside the main mausoleum during the Mughal era. At that time, it was known as the Shahi Darwaza. During British rule, it later came to be called the Royal Gate. SK Kulshrestha, former in-charge of the Taj Mahal and a retired Conservation Assistant with the Archaeological Survey of India, said the stones have naturally weakened with age. According to him, unless high-quality conservation work is carried out, stones will continue to crack and fall. He explained that conservation work was earlier handled directly by the department, with engineers carefully considering the monument’s historical characteristics. However, most restoration work is now contractor-driven. He believes contractors often lack the specialised expertise required for heritage conservation, which has affected the quality of repair work. Kulshrestha also pointed to the unavailability of traditional construction materials as a major concern. Earlier conservation work used pebble lime and specially prepared mortar containing strengthening compounds. Such materials are now difficult to obtain. Taj Mahal generates more than Rs 100 crore annually Despite repeated increases in ticket prices, tourist interest in the Taj Mahal remains extremely high. The monument continues to generate the highest revenue among sites protected by the Archaeological Survey of India. At present- An additional Rs 200 ticket is required to enter the main dome area. As a result, Indian visitors spend Rs 250 to view the complete monument, while foreign tourists pay Rs 1,300. Know the income for each year According to ASI data, offline ticket sales alone generated Rs 105 crore 49 lakh 12 thousand 855 during the financial years 2024-25 and 2025-26 combined. Including online ticket sales, the total revenue exceeded Rs 200 crore. Even after ticket prices increased over the decades, from just 20 paise to Rs 250 for Indian visitors, tourist numbers have not seen any major decline. Ticket system introduced in 1966 Entry to the Taj Mahal remained completely free until 1966. That year, a ticketing system was introduced for the first time, with tickets priced at just 20 paise. Today, a tiered pricing structure is followed to regulate the growing number of tourists, with separate rates for different categories of visitors. How ticket prices increased Concerns over conservation spending Concerns are also being raised over the amount spent on conservation compared with the monument’s earnings. Not only the Royal Gate, but several other sections of the Taj Mahal complex have also deteriorated over time. Stones continue to break and fall from various parts of the monument. Despite the monument generating hundreds of crores in revenue, ASI data shows that approximately Rs 5 crore was spent on conservation work at the Taj Mahal during the last financial year. Kalander Bind said that conservation work is being carried out regularly and that restoration projects worth around Rs 5 crore have been completed at the monument.

stories.title: Are police killings of child-crime suspects revealing a pattern?:UP witnesses three such shooting deaths in a month
stories.summary: On May 5 in Hardoi, a 7-year-old child was allegedly sexually assaulted and murdered, triggering outrage across Uttar Pradesh. Within 12 hours, police killed the accused, Mehnoor, in an encounter. The incident reflects a shifting pattern in UP Police action, where encounters are increasingly being used not only against mafia and crimes against women, but also against those accused of crimes against children. Know what kind of crimes the police were strict about earlier What is the latest pattern? Taking action on crimes against children within hours 4 recent major incidents show that the police are taking very aggressive action against those who commit crimes against children. How the Yogi government worked in 9 years Focus on organised crime After Yogi Adityanath became Chief Minister in 2017, curbing organised crime became a major focus. In the first 10 months of his government, UP Police carried out 1,142 encounters in which 34 criminals were killed. The first encounter was of Gurmeet in Saharanpur on March 31, 2017. Later, police killed Naushad and Sarwar in Shamli on July 29. Naushad had 19 serious criminal cases against him, while Sarwar had 8. Ikram was killed in an encounter on August 10, followed by Nadeem on September 8 and Shamshad on September 10. Cracked down on crimes against women 'Operation Langda' launched Police adopted a strategy of psychological pressure for those who molested or committed violence against women and daughters. Videos were released showing the accused with bandages on their legs (limping) and apologizing. This sent a message that those who molest or rape women will not be spared. 2019-21: Taught lessons to those who attacked the uniform Encounter for murder or assault of police 2024: Action on those who commit major robberies 25 encounters in one year 2025: Contract killers killed 48 encounters in 2025 This year, a maximum of 48 criminals were killed in encounters. Especially, contract killers were the target of UP Police. Among them, Banarasi Yadav of Varanasi was the main one. 24 cases were registered against him. More than half of these were for contract killings. UPSTF killed him in Chaubepur. Similarly, STF encountered Mohammad Rehan of Shamli, accused in 90 cases. Ashu alias Monty of Moradabad was considered a sharpshooter. STF and Moradabad Police killed him in an encounter. Read what Retired IPS Lalji Shukla says Question: When and how does the police pattern against crime change? Retired IPS: Police strategy changes with changing crime patterns. Around 20 years ago, organized crime and highway robberies were common. Later, criminals began looting families at gunpoint inside homes and even firing at police during encounters. Crimes against women and children are highly emotional issues, and public anger rises sharply in such cases. With CCTV cameras now common, incidents are often captured on video, increasing pressure on police to act quickly. As crime patterns evolve, police response also changes accordingly. Question: How can this model benefit the UP elections? Retired IPS: People want to feel safe and usually support governments that provide security. With elections approaching, the Yogi government will likely try to further strengthen this law-and-order image. The impact of UP model on the Bengal elections After BJP's victory in West Bengal, the 'UP Police Model' is in the headlines. PM Modi, Home Minister Amit Shah, and CM Yogi explained to the public during the campaign how the mafia rule was ended in UP. How were state borders secured? On this, Mamata Banerjee had to say that Bengal does not need any 'external model'. The agenda of Maa-Maati-Manush (Mother, Soil, People) is fine.

stories.title: Prayagraj murder case:Class 9 student Khushi’s skeletal remains gorged by animals, found in bush 17 days after murder
stories.summary: The carcass of a class nine student was found in a bushy area, 17 days after her murder, allegedly by her 17-year-old boyfriend in Prayagraj. Animals gorged on the skeletal remains of the rotten body. The family could find only her clothes and bones at the post-mortem house. Her mother, Sunita Pal, fainted upon seeing the body was in such a bad state. After regaining consciousness, she kept screaming. I want revenge. One life is gone, I want four lives in return. I want the lives of the killer, his family, and his maternal uncle. Khushboo, the elder sister of Khushi Pal, who was killed by her boyfriend, said, The murderer should be hanged. The entire family conspired to commit the murder. His family deserves the same. The boy's maternal uncle, maternal aunt, mother, and father are all involved in this murder. Khushi's sister Muskan said, We came to know about their affair a month ago. Our family had explained it to the boy. Then he told me to tell my sister to either choose him or choose the family. The person who killed my sister should receive the harshest possible punishment. Accused's family fled Since the arrest of the accused student, father Suresh Verma, mother Seema, and younger brother Apurva have been absconding. The house is locked. Relatives and neighbors living around the house cannot believe that a boy studying in intermediate can commit such a heinous murder. The accused's father Suresh, drives his own auto. Neighbor Sanjeev Verma said that the whole village knew he was a simple boy. No one thought he would commit murder. Sanjeev says he always kept to himself. He didn't talk much to people. Ria, named in the FIR When Khushi Pal ran away from home, her mother Sunita Pal named a girl named Ria Patel along with the lover. After the murder case came to light, the police also took Ria into custody. She was interrogated for a long time. Ria kept crying at the police station after being caught. Riya's important role in the love story Khushi's sister Khushboo says that Riya Patel is the accused's classmate. The accused introduced her to Khushi by making her his adopted sister. All conversations and meetings with Khushi happened through Riya. Khushi had saved Riya's number in her mobile. Friendship started on Instagram The distance between the ancestral homes of the accused and the girl is about 30 kilometers. Their friendship started on Instagram. Then they started looking for excuses to meet. In this crucial link, a house came in handy. Khushi's aunt's house is in Araipur Soraon. While the boy's maternal grandmother's house is right next door. Just by talking, both started living at their relatives' houses. They started meeting through their classmate Riya Patel. Khushi wanted to have a love marriage Both families were strict due to them being minors. Khushi wanted to have a love marriage. After this, she even talked to a relative who was a lawyer. Later, the boy's maternal uncle and others opposed it and stopped the matter. Understand the whole matter Khushi (17), daughter of auto driver Laxmi Narayan Pal, a resident of Jamunipur village, had an affair with a boy (17) from the Baharia area. Khushi was the second of 4 sisters. She studied in class 9 at Motilal Inter College in the same village. When both families came to know about their closeness, they explained to the children and asked them to stay away. When he didn't agree, the girl's family members also beat the young man. Meanwhile, Khushi kept pressuring him for marriage. To get rid of Khushi, the boy made a plan to murder her. He called Khushi to meet him during the day on April 20. Both decided that they would run away from home. According to the plan, the accused ran away from home with Khushi at night. Then, near the Sharda feeder canal, he stabbed her multiple times with a knife. He strangled her with a dupatta. Then he threw the body and fled.

stories.title: Rain and thunderstorm warning across 28 UP districts:Jalaun receives showers; temperatures drop, weather to change from tomorrow
stories.summary: The spell of storms and rain in UP has continued for the seventh straight day. On Friday morning, Jalaun witnessed rain and strong winds, with dark clouds covering the sky. Weather remained clear in Lucknow, Kanpur, Noida, and Ghaziabad, with bright sunshine and cooler conditions due to humidity, though temperatures are expected to rise later in the day. The Meteorological Department has issued a storm and rain alert for 28 districts, with lightning likely in some areas. The rain spell, ongoing since April 30, has brought major relief from heat, reducing maximum temperatures by up to 10°C. Banda, which recorded 47.6°C on April 28, saw temperatures fall to 38°C by May 7. On Thursday, rain lashed 15 districts, including Lucknow, Kanpur, and Barabanki, while Mahoba saw hailstorm and rain for nearly half an hour. In Bijnor, a CCTV tower collapsed during the storm. In Barabanki, slippery roads caused a collision involving several vehicles, including two double-decker buses, leaving one person dead. Jalaun in Bundelkhand recorded the state’s highest rainfall at 27 mm. Atul Kumar Singh, Senior Scientist at the Regional Meteorological Centre, Lucknow, stated: The active western disturbance of the past week is now weakening. Today, scattered rain may occur in eastern and western UP. There is a possibility of thunderstorms and lightning. From tomorrow, the heat will show its intensity. The mercury will start rising again. However, relief from heatwave will continue for now. Weather pictures Know the condition of the cities- Why are there weather fluctuations? The Meteorological Department says that the weather in the mountains of Uttarakhand is constantly changing. Snowfall is occurring. There is an alert for rain and snowfall for the next 2 to 3 days as well. Its direct impact is visible in UP. Winds coming from the mountains are keeping the weather cool. They are creating systems favorable for rain. Weather forecast for the next 5 days

stories.title: UP cabinet expansion may reflect smart meter anger:AK Sharma could be shunted out of energy ministry
stories.summary: The UP government’s rollback on smart prepaid meters came amid rising public anger and growing anti-government sentiment. RSS and BJP leaders reportedly warned that not reversing the decision could hurt the party in the upcoming assembly elections. Now, high-level sources in the RSS and BJP say the Energy Department may be taken away from Energy Minister AK Sharma during the next cabinet expansion. 5 reasons for anger over smart prepaid meters 1. Postpaid meters converted to prepaid without consent: There are about 3.58 crore domestic electricity consumers in UP. By February 2026, smart meters were installed in 87 lakh of these homes. Of these, 82 lakh were smart postpaid meters. The department converted them into prepaid meters. This work started in January. After this, from March-April, the electricity department started disconnecting electricity connections for arrears. 2. Electricity disconnected for 5 lakh homes simultaneously: The real trouble started after this. The department disconnected electricity for more than 5 lakh homes simultaneously, citing a negative balance. Even after recharging, the supply did not resume. When people protested, the department clarified that it happened due to a technical issue. 3. Apprehensions regarding smart meters: Many videos went viral claiming that consumption was being recorded in smart prepaid meters even without an electricity connection. A common perception was formed that these meters run fast. The department could not dispel this notion. 4. No system for complaints: People complained that electricity bills were many times higher than the average. The department had no system to hear complaints. Complaints made on helpline 1912 were closed without resolution. 5. Net meters of solar plants removed: Even the net meters installed at the premises of consumers who had solar panels were replaced with smart prepaid meters. Then, their hefty bills were sent without deducting the electricity generated from solar. Understand how the decision to withdraw was made Public protests increased concern The BJP failed to gauge public anger over prepaid meters, while the SP and other opposition parties could not turn it into a political issue. As a result, people across UP united and protested on their own. Protests spread from Lucknow to Agra, Firozabad, Varanasi, Prayagraj, Hapur, Bareilly, and Mathura without any central leadership. Middle-class women even removed meters and protested outside electricity offices, with videos quickly going viral. As the issue escalated, CM Yogi Adityanath formed an expert committee to investigate smart meters. However, public anger continued, with fears it could fuel anti-incumbency against the government. Narrative was building against govt in election year A source associated with the Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh says that despite widespread protests, the government did not want to withdraw its decision. Officials had convinced those in the government that people were protesting under the influence of some individuals. However, in the coordination meeting between the Sangh and the government, Sangh officials intervened. The Sangh said that the government should handle this matter as soon as possible. Meanwhile, the BJP organization was continuously receiving negative feedback from MLAs and BJP leaders regarding Energy Minister AK Sharma. Leaders from districts like Agra, Aligarh, Firozabad had made it clear that if the decision was not reversed, this issue would become a major problem in the elections. Opposition becoming active due to public protests Given the increasing protests across UP, political rhetoric had started from the Samajwadi Party (SP), Congress, and Aam Aadmi Party (AAP). Akhilesh Yadav had compared smart meters to EVMs. He had said- This is a big scam. Just as EVMs are not understood by people, smart meters are also a means of plunder. Akhilesh had even said that if the SP government is formed, 300 units of free electricity will be provided. After this, AAP's Rajya Sabha MP and UP in-charge Sanjay Singh had said- Smart meters are now looting the public by becoming 'smart cheaters'. Their speed has become faster than even Milkha Singh. Decision suddenly changed after results of 5 states On May 4, election results were announced in 5 states and union territories of the country. In West Bengal, TMC lost and BJP came to power for the first time. Seeing the changing equations, Energy Minister AK Sharma suddenly reached Shakti Bhawan on May 4 itself. After meeting with officials, he announced the abolition of the prepaid system. Now, consumers will again receive monthly bills. The facility to pay outstanding bills in installments has also been provided. The Energy Minister said - 'Consumer is God'. This decision has been taken considering technical difficulties and consumer complaints. Along with this, instructions were given that electricity should not be disconnected under any circumstances within one month. Smart meter flaws not rectified even in 3 years Energy Efficiency Services Limited (EESL), a Government of India company, had installed 1.2 million smart meters in UP in 2023. Even then, there was a lot of controversy surrounding it. Following this, the Government of India sent a high-level inquiry committee. The committee visited different parts of UP to understand the smart metering system, billing system, and consumer experience. Its report revealed several serious flaws related to smart meters. These have not been rectified even after 3 years.

stories.title: Govt issues order to convert prepaid meters to postpaid:Allows customers to pay power bills up to April in 10 installments
stories.summary: The Uttar Pradesh government has decided to convert prepaid smart electricity meters into postpaid meters. On Thursday, UP Power Corporation Managing Director Nitish Kumar issued instructions to all distribution divisions regarding the change. Following these directions, the electricity bill for May consumption, which will be issued in June, will now be on a postpaid basis. Bills will continue to be generated on the 10th of every month as usual. According to the corporation’s order, consumers will be allowed to pay the postpaid security deposit in four equal installments. Outstanding electricity dues can also be cleared in ten equal installments. The first installment of the security deposit must be paid in June along with the bill generated for May’s electricity usage. Consumers will receive their electricity bills through SMS and WhatsApp. Know what instructions were given in the order? Postpaid security amount will have to be paid in four installments According to the Chairman of Power Corporation, during the conversion to prepaid mode, the postpaid security amount was transferred to the balance. Now, due to switching back to postpaid, the security amount will have to be deposited in 4 installments as per the 'Cost Data Book-2026' and based on the sanctioned load. The first installment will have to be deposited with the bill to be issued in June. The other three installments will have to be deposited in the next three months. The RMS will issue this itself. Apart from this, as before, consumers will be given 15 days to deposit the bill. After this, a disconnection date of 7 days will be given. This will also be marked on the bill. As before, if any consumer is unable to deposit the bill by the due date, they will also have to pay a penalty. Outstanding bills till April can be deposited in 10 installments For the convenience of domestic consumers, the Power Corporation has provided the facility to deposit outstanding electricity bills in 10 installments along with a surcharge till 30th April. Consumers of other categories will have to deposit the outstanding amount in 3 installments in the ratio of 40%, 30%, 30%. Special camps from 15th May for bill complaints The Chairman has ordered all electricity companies to address the numerous complaints from people regarding outstanding bill amounts. For their resolution, special camps will be organized from 15th May to 30th June at the offices of all Executive Engineers and Sub-Divisional Officers. Apart from this, special arrangements are also being made for the 1912 helpline number. Why did the government have to discontinue the prepaid system? Electricity consumers say that smart meters run very fast. Due to this, higher bills are coming even with less usage. In fact, many times the balance decreases even without usage. As soon as the balance goes into minus, the electricity supply gets disconnected. Even after a recharge, the supply is often not restored immediately. On Sunday, protests regarding smart meters took place in Agra, Prayagraj, Kanpur, Lucknow, Fatehpur, and Varanasi. In Fatehpur, electricity consumers had uprooted smart meters and thrown them at the power house. In Agra, women uprooted smart meters from their homes and threw them on the streets. They said that we don't want smart meters, we want the old meters. After the installation of smart meters, electricity bills have been coming higher. Money is being deposited in advance. Even after depositing money, electricity is being cut. When inquired, they say that the balance is in minus.

The BJP defended the PM's call as responsible leadership and national interest.

stories.summary: Dubai has launched its first fully integrated smart bus station at Mall of the Emirates, enhancing commuter experience with AI and digital services. The station signifies Dubai's commitment to modernizing public transport with smart infrastructure.

President Trump has rejected these terms as unacceptable. The standoff has impacted global oil markets and heightened regional tensions. Diplomatic efforts continue amidst ongoing clashes.

stories.title: Vijay's first day as CM and a Tamil Nadu song row: What happened?
stories.summary: Tamil Nadu's chief minister's swearing-in ceremony sparked controversy as the state song 'Tamil Thaai Vaazhthu' was placed third, after the national song and anthem. This deviation from tradition, where the state song usually begins government events, drew strong objections from CPI and the ruling TVK party, which vowed to revert to the established practice.

stories.title: Rahul Gandhi calls PM Modi's 'don't buy gold for a year, WFH' appeal 'proof of failure'

stories.summary: Congress leader Shashi Tharoor raised concerns about the 2026 West Bengal assembly elections, suggesting the Special Intensive Revision of electoral rolls may have influenced the BJP's victory. He highlighted the removal of 91 lakh names, with 34 lakh appeals pending adjudication, questioning the fairness of the process given the BJP's 30 lakh vote margin.

stories.title: Did govt block Rahul Gandhi's Instagram reel with Vijay? What ministry said
stories.summary: The Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology has denied blocking Rahul Gandhi's social media posts featuring Tamil Nadu Chief Minister Vijay. Sources stated that Instagram's internal system mistakenly flagged the content, which has since been restored. This clarification comes after Congress alleged the ministry was suppressing opposition voices.

stories.title: Daily wage earners 31% of all suicide deaths in 2024, highest in a decade: NCRB
stories.summary: Daily wage earners constituted 31% of all suicide deaths in 2024, the highest in a decade, with 52,910 such fatalities. This marks a significant increase from previous years, as the total number of suicides nationwide rose to 1.7 lakh. Family problems and illness remain the primary reported causes for these tragic deaths.

stories.title: "Trying to ruin the life of Erika": Laura Loomer accuses Candace Owens of pushing “bankrupt” lies while harassing Erika Kirk
stories.summary: Candace Owens and Laura Loomer reignited their public feud on X with a series of deeply personal accusations. Loomer accused Owens of living a luxurious lifestyle while falsely claiming financial struggles, while Owens responded with harsh remarks about Loomer’s mental health and public reputation. The argument later escalated when Loomer brought Erika Kirk into the dispute, accusing Owens of targeting her and spreading lies about others online.

stories.title: Who is Amos Yee? Controversial Singapore YouTuber assaulted by Yuji Itadori cosplayer outside anime convention
stories.summary: Controversial Singaporean YouTuber Amos Yee was reportedly assaulted outside the Doujima anime convention in Singapore by an 18-year-old dressed as Yuji Itadori. Videos online showed the cosplayer punching and kicking Yee during the altercation. The incident came after convention organisers banned Yee from entering the event. Following the attack, Yee blamed the organisers for escalating tensions and denied rumours accusing him of inappropriate behaviour at the venue.

stories.title: ‘Healthy and asymptomatic’: Indian Embassy says crew members evacuated from hantavirus-hit MV Hondius are safe
stories.summary: Two Indian crew members aboard the hantavirus-hit MV Hondius have been evacuated to the Netherlands for quarantine, confirmed healthy and asymptomatic by the Indian Embassy in Spain. The Dutch-flagged vessel experienced an outbreak after anchoring off the Canary Islands. The WHO advised a risk-based approach for managing contacts, noting limited human-to-human transmission of the Andes virus.

stories.title: After big wins, NDA sitting comfortably for 2027 presidential election
'Need to save foreign exchange amid war crisis': PM Modi pushes for cut in fuel use & gold buying, favours WFH
stories.summary: Amid global energy disruptions, PM Modi urged Indians to conserve foreign exchange by reducing reliance on imported fuel. He advocated for public transport, work-from-home, avoiding overseas trips and non-essential gold purchases for a year. The Prime Minister also encouraged farmers to halve chemical fertilizer use and shift towards natural farming.

stories.title: India, UAE working on pact to help in evacuation of Indians via Fujairah port
stories.summary: India and UAE are finalizing an agreement to facilitate the evacuation of Indian workers via Fujairah port, a move likely to be signed during PM Modi's upcoming stopover. This pact addresses potential disruptions from the West Asia conflict, offering a crucial maritime route for over 4 million Indian workers in the UAE.

stories.title: Kolkata flips, BJP leads in 102 of 144 civic wards
stories.summary: BJP's strong performance in Kolkata's assembly elections, leading in 102 of 144 KMC wards, has sparked speculation about advancing municipal polls. Police have assessed the security at the palatial building, constructed for VVIPs. Adhikari, who has emphasized accessibility at his ancestral home, may opt for the more centralized Soujanya due to security needs.

stories.summary: NTPC is preparing to submit a feasibility report to the Centre for its first nuclear energy plant, aiming to contribute to India's goal of 100 GW atomic power capacity by 2047. The company has identified land in Bihar and plans to set up 30 GW of nuclear capacity across 14 states by 2047, with initial units of 700 MW each.

stories.summary: India's space commercial arm, NSIL, is poised for a significant shift as a private sector leader, reportedly from Boeing, is the front-runner for its CMD post. British surveyors used this ridge for the Great Trigonometrical Survey, fixing coordinates and calculating distances that helped measure Mount Everest. Today, this historically significant site lies neglected, with its structures vandalized and stones stolen.

stories.summary: Bangladesh High Court rejected a bail plea for Hindu monk Chinmoy Krishna Das in a lawyer's killing case. He is already facing trial for sedition, having been denied bail previously. The court will hear bail petitions for four other cases against the monk on Monday.

stories.title: Israel operated from Iraq's Najaf desert during war: Reports
stories.summary: Israeli forces reportedly established a temporary base on an old airstrip in Iraq's Najaf desert during the war against Iran, according to security officials. The operation, coordinated with the US, led to clashes with Iraqi troops. While no forces remain, equipment may have been left behind. Iraq had previously protested an air raid in the area.

stories.title: Non-binary Indian on student visa elected to Scottish Parliament
stories.summary: A non-binary transgender Indian national, Q Manivannan, has been elected as a Member of the Scottish Parliament (MSP) on a student visa. stories.summary: Singapore's cultural festival saw Indian mangoes as the star attraction, with performers receiving boxes of the prized fruit. stories.title: Inside ‘mommy brain’: How pregnancy and childbirth rewire the maternal mind
stories.summary: Pregnancy and childbirth trigger significant physiological, psychological, and emotional transformations in women, often leading to "mommy brain" characterized by forgetfulness and mental fog. Scientific studies reveal neural recalibration, not decline, as the brain adapts to caregiving demands. This experience, while common, requires understanding and support for new mothers navigating identity shifts and cognitive loads.

Her powerful voice, first heard in 'Ek Se Badhkar Ek,' has been a constant amidst political shifts. Receiving the Minar-e-Dilli award, she emphasized music's healing power, a sentiment echoed by fans who find solace in her melodies.

'Money’s all there': Stalin reacts to Vijay’s first speech, says Tamil Nadu debt 'well within permissible limits'

Stalin refuted this, stating the state's debt is within limits and urging Vijay not to start his tenure with such claims. Vijay vowed transparency and prioritizing public welfare.

stories.title: 'Vile, brazen & mischievous': CJI Surya Kant slams casteist remarks attributed to him on social media
stories.summary: Chief Justice of India Surya Kant has vehemently denied a fabricated social media quote attributed to him, calling the act "vile, brazen and mischievous." The CJI stated that manufacturing and attributing such a quote to the highest judicial office is an act of dishonesty and social incitement.

stories.title: RSS’s long march in Bengal culminates in BJP’s triumph
stories.summary: Decades of groundwork by the RSS and its expanding social and organizational networks in West Bengal have reshaped the state's political landscape, culminating in the BJP's electoral breakthrough. This patient, years-long outreach, rooted in identity and community, gradually converted scattered support into a cohesive political force, leading to a decisive electoral victory.

stories.summary: C. Joseph Vijay was sworn in as the new Chief Minister of Tamil Nadu on Sunday, marking a significant political shift. Prime Minister Narendra Modi congratulated Vijay and assured continued central government support for the state's welfare. Vijay's party, TVK, secured victory in the 2026 elections, ending the dominance of Dravidian parties.

stories.summary: C Joseph Vijay has become the new Chief Minister of Tamil Nadu. He took the oath of office along with his cabinet members. This marks the formal assumption of power by the Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam party. The party achieved a significant electoral victory on May 4. This win ended the long-standing dominance of traditional Dravidian parties.

stories.title: Mother’s Day: After losing 2 sons, army jawan’s wife donates part of her liver to save 8-year-old son
